observations.statement: Redefining E as Midpoint(D, C + (1, 0)) is rejected as ambiguous although the expression is semantically unambiguous.
observations.originatingSeam: durable dependency projection during redefine assessment
observations.rootCause: Publication and redefine assessment use the same direct projection over the parent algorithm's inputs with opposite null handling: publication drops inputs without a persistent identity, assessment throws. The thrown IllegalArgumentException is caught and reported as the AMBIGUOUS assessment status before cycle analysis, host-shape checking, compatible-redefine inspection, impact analysis and any legacy offer.
observations.corollary: Because D is unregistered independently of the edit, any redefine of E - including re-entering the identical Midpoint(D, C) - takes the same throw.
observations.naiveFixInsufficient: Dropping nulls on both sides leaves E's candidate dependency set empty, unequal to the stored {C}, so the non-public dependency-set gate rejects on both the retain and the replacement inspection, yielding UNSUPPORTED. Only a transitive closure through the unregistered helper restores {C}; that is a genuinely new third rule and must be adopted on both sides together.

observations.statement: Nine distinct IllegalArgumentException causes collapse onto the single AMBIGUOUS assessment status, so a correct rejection such as a geo-family change is reported as ambiguity.
